title: Expert Support Technique et Comptable (Télétravail complet possible - Limousin / Dordogne / Lot-et-Garonne)
descriptionHtml:
Vous cherchez un environnement professionnel stimulant basé sur l'autonomie et la confiance ?

Pennylane vous offre l'opportunité de grandir au sein d'une entreprise en pleine croissance.

Ici, votre expertise contribuera directement à aider les entrepreneurs à reprendre le contrôle de leurs finances. Découvrez un lieu où vos compétences seront valorisées et où vous pourrez façonner l'avenir de la gestion financière.

Notre vision

Notre ambition est de devenir le logiciel de pilotage financier préféré des PMEs européennes.

Nous aidons les entrepreneurs à se débarrasser des tâches chronophages liées à la comptabilité et à la finance, tout en leur donnant accès à des informations financières clés pour les aider à prendre les meilleures décisions pour leur entreprise.

Parallèlement, nous aidons les cabinets d'expertise-comptable, en leur permettant de passer moins de temps sur des tâches redondantes et répétitives, et plus de temps sur la partie conseil et accompagnement de leurs clients.

À propos de Pennylane

Pennylane est une des FinTech à la plus forte croissance en France, et souhaite bientôt adresser le marché européen.

En 6 ans d'existence, nous sommes parvenus à :

💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant

💰 Lever un total de 400 millions d'euros, auprès d'investisseurs de renom, dont Sequoïa, le fonds phare de la Silicon Valley, connu pour avoir soutenu Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal et bien d'autres à leur début

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Passer de 7 cofondateurs à une équipe de 1000 collaborateurs, avec une note moyenne de 4,9/5 sur Glassdoor et 94% des évaluateurs Glassdoor qui recommanderaient PL à leurs proches!

🌍 Construire une équipe internationale composée de collaborateurs issus de 25 pays différents, avec une culture du télétravail très flexible

🤝 Gagner la confiance de milliers d'utilisateurs et obtenir d'excellents retours

🚀 Déjà plus de 1 million de TPE/PME et plus de 7 000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France !

Tu as une solide expérience en comptabilité et tu aimes comprendre comment fonctionnent les outils SaaS ?
Tu souhaites intervenir sur des problématiques complexes, à la frontière entre métier, produit et technologie ?
Rejoins Pennylane en tant qu’Expert·e Support Technique et Comptable.

Ton rôle
Tu prends en charge les sujets les plus complexes remontés par nos utilisateurs et nos équipes Support.
Ton objectif : comprendre l’origine des problèmes, qu’ils soient comptables, fonctionnels ou techniques, puis coordonner leur résolution avec les équipes Produit et Tech.
Tu joueras un rôle clé entre les utilisateurs, le Support, les développeurs et les équipes Produit.

Tes missions

  • Investiguer des bugs, anomalies et problématiques comptables ou fonctionnelles.

  • Reproduire les problèmes rencontrés et en identifier la cause.

  • Qualifier les incidents et coordonner leur résolution avec les équipes concernées.

  • Échanger avec les développeurs et le Produit pour transmettre des analyses claires et exploitables.

  • Utiliser les outils d’investigation disponibles : logs et SQL simple.

  • Documenter les solutions et contribuer à l’amélioration continue du produit et des process.

  • Partager ton expertise avec les équipes Support.


Le profil recherché

Tu peux venir de différents environnements : cabinet d’expertise comptable ou éditeur de logiciel comptable.

Nous recherchons une personne qui :

  • dispose d’une solide expérience en comptabilité et comprend les problématiques des cabinets et entreprises ;

  • a déjà travaillé sur des sujets complexes nécessitant analyse et coordination ;

  • est à l’aise avec les outils et problématiques techniques ;

  • sait communiquer clairement avec des interlocuteurs métiers et techniques ;

  • parle anglais dans un contexte professionnel, à l’écrit comme à l’oral ;

  • fait preuve de rigueur, d’autonomie et de curiosité.

La connaissance de SQL est un plus, mais n’est pas indispensable. Ce qui compte surtout, c’est ton envie de comprendre les systèmes et de monter en compétence sur les sujets techniques.

Pourquoi rejoindre Pennylane ?

Tu rejoindras une équipe au cœur de la qualité produit, en lien direct avec les utilisateurs, les développeurs et les équipes Produit. Tu travailleras dans un environnement international, en forte croissance, où ton expertise comptable aura un impact concret

Process de recrutement :

  • Premier échange un/e recruteur - 30 min

  • Étude de cas et debriefing avec deux membres de l’équipe - 60 min

  • Entretien avec le Manager direct - Thibault et Viviane (Associate Team Lead Technical Support) - 60 min

  • Entretien avec Thomas (Team Lead Technical Support) - 45 min

🎁 Ce que l’on peut t'offrir :

🏥 Une mutuelle parmi les meilleures sur le marché (Alan Blue et Alan Mind)

🍜 Des tickets restaurants (Carte Swile)

🏝 Entre 6 et 12 jours de RTT supplémentaires aux 5 semaines de congés payés

🇬🇧 La possibilité de perfectionner ton anglais grâce à Busuu

🧑‍💻 Un budget dédié chaque mois pour tous nos Pennylaners, favorisant le travail depuis la maison ou en espace de coworking

🏢 Une facilité d’accès à nos bureaux, situés à quelques minutes de Saint Lazare en plein cœur de Paris

💵 Une enveloppe de BSPCE

🏃‍♀️ Un accès à 8000 salles de sport partout en France et plus de 300 activités de bien-être via notre partenaire Gymlib

💻 Un Mac

🎉 Nous pratiquons de nombreux sports ensemble et avons à cœur de nous réunir régulièrement autour d’événements d’entreprise tels que les Tech Days (qui permettent aux Pennylaners en remote de se réunir tous les 3 mois) ou notre séminaire d’entreprise qui a lieu une fois par an, et qui favorise de grands moments de cohésion pour toutes et tous.

Pour t'épanouir chez Pennylane, il faudra:

  • Parler anglais (le niveau est évalué et apprécié en fonction du département auquel tu postules)

  • Apprécier travailler dans un environnement en changement constant

  • Faire de la collaboration une priorité au sein de son équipe ou avec d'autres parties prenantes

  • Avoir un recul suffisant pour prioriser les actions à fort impact business dans son activité quotidienne.

Nous savons que certaines personnes sont moins susceptibles de postuler que d'autres si elles estiment ne pas remplir l'intégralité des critères.

Si tu hésites, nous t'encourageons à postuler quand même : qui sait, cela pourrait être le début d'une collaboration significative et durable !

Information importante à destination des candidat(e)s

Les tentatives d’arnaque au recrutement sont en hausse. Nous vous invitons à rester vigilant(e) lors de vos échanges.

Candidature uniquement via nos canaux officiels : postulez exclusivement via nos offres publiées sur nos supports officiels (site carrière, pages officielles partenaires).

Vérifiez systématiquement l’adresse e-mail de l’expéditeur : nos communications sont envoyées depuis des adresses professionnelles avec les domaine @pennylane.com ou @pennylane-partners.com .

Nous ne vous demanderons jamais de paiement, ni d’informations financières (coordonnées bancaires, paiement pour un entretien, achat de matériel, etc.) dans le cadre du recrutement.

Si une telle demande vous est faite, il s’agit d’une fraude. Nous vous invitons à ne pas répondre et à nous le signaler immédiatement."

Encourageant la diversité, équité et inclusion sous toutes ses formes, Pennylane offre un environnement de travail inclusif, bienveillant et propice à l’épanouissement, dans nos bureaux et en remote. Nous nous engageons à fournir les mêmes chances à tous nos candidats, indépendamment de leurs origines sociales et ethniques, genres, religions, orientations sexuelles ou handicaps.

🇫🇷 Données personnelles

Pennylane traite vos données pour gérer votre candidature et évaluer votre adéquation au poste. Vous pouvez vous opposer à tout moment et demander la suppression de vos données en écrivant à :

Pennylane processes your data to manage your application and assess your suitability for the position. If your application is unsuccessful, your data may be retained for 2 years from our last exchange or the closing of the recruitment process, in order to build and manage a candidate pool. You may object at any time and request the deletion of your data by writing to Learn more

Pennylane verarbeitet Ihre Daten, um Ihre Bewerbung zu bearbeiten und Ihre Eignung für die Stelle zu beurteilen. title: Factory Advisor (Deployed Factory Engineer)
descriptionHtml:
About Isembard

Isembard is building a network of high-performance factories for critical industries. We combine advanced machine tools, robotics and our own software, MasonOS, to make precision components for aerospace, defence, energy and frontier technology companies, with factories across the UK, US, Germany and France. Our mission is to forge industrial acceleration.

The role

A factory network is only as good as its worst site. Factory Advisors, sometimes called deployed factory engineers, get new and existing sites in our network running to the Isembard standard and keep them there.

You will deploy into factories, work directly with owner-operators, general managers and site teams, and be their point of contact as they become operationally and financially successful. Technical competence matters, but communication is the differentiator: you learn the operating playbook in depth, teach it clearly and hold every site to it.

What you'll do

  • Support factory setup, onboarding and operating-model implementation at new and existing sites.

  • Translate the playbook into shop-floor practice: production flow, documentation, quality and traceability, communication cadence and MasonOS adoption.

  • Train site teams and explain technical concepts in language people can act on.

  • Audit factories against the playbook, write clear findings and corrective action plans, and recommend go or no-go when a site is not ready.

  • Help site owners understand their P&L and cash flow, and improve profitability.

What we're looking for

  • Strong operating experience in a demanding, practical environment.

  • Outstanding written and verbal communication.

  • Technical curiosity and the ability to learn systems quickly.

  • The judgement to hold a high bar without losing the room.

  • The ability to analyse a P&L and cash flow statement.

Nice to have

  • Implementing SOPs, quality systems, training programmes or site audits.

  • Process engineering or factory operations.

  • Military operations or logistics.

  • Manufacturing, CNC, aerospace or defence, and exposure to AS9100, ITAR or export control.

Why Isembard

  • Directly affect how well factories launch, operate and improve.

  • Work across advanced machine tools, MasonOS, quality systems and live production.

title: Financial Crime Investigator
descriptionHtml:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role:

  • We’re hiring new financial crime investigators due to continued business growth.

  • You’ll conduct important financial crime screening checks and investigations into new applicants and existing customers.

  • You will use screening tools to match customer data against PEPs & Sanctions lists and use your initiative to determine the risks associated with the application/ customer.

  • You will review customer profile information and transactional activity to identify financial crime risks, and take appropriate action on the account..

  • You will submit internal Suspicious Activity Reports in instances where suspicious activity has been identified. 

  • As the business grows you may be required to take on additional tasks to support the Financial Crime Team.

  • You’ll work in the office 3 days per week.

  • You'll work 40 hours per week. This means you'll work Monday to Friday, from 9am to 6pm, with a one hour lunch break.

  • You'll also work one full weekend (Saturday and Sunday), once every 4 weeks, and have two weekdays off in lieu.

Your team’s objectives

  • Protect our customers and society, by preventing fraud and financial crime.

  • Comply with financial crime regulations and company policy.

  • Minimise customer and applicant friction through skilled and timely decisions.

  • Identify opportunities for product and process improvement.

How you’ll impact those objectives

  • You’ll support new application checks and existing customer monitoring.

  • You’ll investigate potential Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and Sanctions matches, and assist with onboarding reviews.

  • You’ll monitor activity and transactions on customer accounts.

  • You will help mitigate risk by escalating Financial crime concerns that you have identified during your reviews.

What do you need to succeed in this role?

  • Ability to collaborate effectively within a diverse team.

  • Have an analytical mindset with a good attention to detail.

  • Strong decision-making skills, and excellent writing skills to document decisions. 

  • Can effectively communicate with customers, applicants and senior management, when necessary.

  • Proficient time management skills, comfortable meeting targets and deadlines.

  • Previous financial crime experience is advantageous, particularly around screening and KYC.

  • Experience in identifying opportunities for process improvements and implementing solutions, including the use of automation and AI technologies to enhance efficiency and effectiveness in financial crime prevention.

  • Demonstrated ability to leverage data, machine learning, and AI to develop and optimise strategies for fraud and financial crime detection and prevention.

The interview process

We’re not a corporation so we try our best to get things moving as quickly as possible. For this role we’d expect:

1) A 15 minute Cognitive Assessment

2) A 30 minute call with a member of the Talent team

3) An onsite Interview and Assessment with the Financial Crime Team Leader/Manager

4) Video Interview with the Head of Fraud and Financial Crime

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

  • Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

  • Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members

  • Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations

  • Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations

descriptionHtml:

You own your team's number, and the goal is ambitious: hit the target together, then double it.


What you'll do

  • Lead your team to its number. You help your team hit its target and build the pipeline and habits that let it grow from there.

Our Go-To-Market team will grow significantly over the next year. You'd join early enough to shape how we lead sales, at a point where you can already see it working. Together with our sales leadership, you'll build your team and help define what great sales management looks like at Lio.

title: Forward Deployed Strategist
descriptionHtml:
About NearformNearform is an independent team of data & AI experts, engineers, and designers who build intelligent digital solutions and capability at pace. We create AI-enabled solutions that enhance digital experiences, empower developers, and deliver measurable results. In these ways, we partner with ambitious enterprises to deliver enduring impact.

Our deep expertise in solving the world’s most complex digital problems, along with our collaborative, people-first approach, enables enterprises to build breakthrough products and modernise legacy systems by unleashing the power of AI.

Today, our team of 500 experts in 20+ countries is trusted by leading enterprises including Lululemon, Puma, Sun Life, Starbucks, Travelex, Virgin Media 02, and Walmart. 

We're on a mission to reinvent how our clients work

Most companies are bolting AI onto old processes and hoping for the best. We think that's the wrong way round.

Nearform is on an exciting journey with AI, and we're building a new team to lead it. The team brings together two worlds that rarely meet: the business thinking of a strategy firm and the engineering depth of a company that builds and ships real products. That puts us in a small group of firms that can do both. We work out what should change and we build it.

The Role

Our clients don't all start in the same place. Some know something has to change but have no idea where to start. Others have a clear picture of the future and are ready to build. Most are somewhere in between.

Your job is to work out where each client really is and shape the right solution for them. That could mean helping a leadership team choose which process to tackle first. It could also mean turning a rough idea into something our engineers can build.

This isn't a traditional management consulting role

You won't be writing a strategy deck that sits on a shelf. This is  hands-on work, close to the technology, and focused on results you can see.

Primary Responsibilities:

  •  Get on the ground. Sit with the teams doing the work, whether they're checking customers against sanctions lists or pulling together month-end reports. Learn how it really happens, including the workarounds, the judgement calls and the steps nobody wrote down.
  • Spot the opportunity. Find where AI and automation can change the game, and where a person still needs to make the call.
  • Design what comes next. Work side by side with a forward deployed engineer to shape a better way of working, testing ideas against what can actually be built.
  • Prove the value. Own the business case for each process you redesign. Work out where the value is, put numbers on it, and set up how it will be measured, so that after go-live you can show the client what changed.
  • Make it real. Turn your design into a plan clear enough for our engineering teams to build, then see it go live.
  • Bring people with you. Run workshops, win over frontline staff and make the case to senior leaders.

Between clients, you'll help build what comes next:

  • Help win new work. Join early conversations with prospective clients and help shape proposals that show what's possible.
  • Shape our offer. Turn what you learn on projects into the methods, tools and stories that make the next engagement faster and sharper.
  • Make the team stronger. Share what works, test new ideas and help define how this team operates as it grows.

Experience:

  •  At least 10 years in consulting, business analysis, operations improvement or a similar role.
  • A track record of mapping a business process and redesigning it with real stakeholders.
  • Confidence in front of clients, whether you're running a workshop, interviewing frontline staff or presenting to a broad group of client stakeholders, including the C-suite.
  • Outcomes thinking. You start with the result the client needs, such as faster turnaround, lower cost or fewer errors, and work backwards from there. You judge success by what changes for the business, not by what gets delivered.
  • Commercial sharpness. You've built business cases before and can turn operational improvements into numbers a CFO will believe.
  • Storytelling. You can pull together a clear, compelling storyline for presentations, quarterly business reviews and leadership updates, the kind that gets decisions made.
  • Builder's mindset. You work in short cycles and test ideas quickly. You'll spin up a proof of concept with tools like Claude Cowork, Lovable or Replit to show a client what's possible, rather than waiting for a perfect plan.
  • A solid grasp of what AI and automation can and can't do. You don't need to code, but you'll hold your own with engineers.
  • Sharp writing: you turn messy conversations into a clear document others can act on.
  • Able to spend time on client sites.

Benefits

  • Work flexibly; we appreciate there are more important things in life than work so our flexible working culture allows you to work around what matters - school run, no problem!

Du lernst direkt von Gründern, die schon Unternehmen aufgebaut und skaliert haben.

Die Stelle ist nur als Praktikum in Vollzeit möglich, mit Start im April 2027 und einer Dauer von idealerweise 6 Monaten.

Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle von Produkt, Vertrieb und Kunde, direkt mit den Gründern. Konkret:

  • Baue Demos, bei denen CPOs aufhorchen. Du entwickelst präzise, maßgeschneiderte Demos, die die Fähigkeiten unserer Agents in ein klares "Das brauchen wir" übersetzen, aufgebaut auf den echten Daten und echten Problemen des Interessenten statt auf einem generischen Durchklicken.

  • Bring Proof of Values zum Erfolg. Du begleitest den POV vom Kickoff bis zum Ergebnis: Du definierst vorab, was "Erfolg" bedeutet, hältst den Kunden engagiert, findest heraus, was nicht funktioniert, und lieferst einen Business Case, den der Kunde intern vertreten kann.

  • Verantworte Product Discovery von Anfang bis Ende. Du bereitest Kundeninterviews vor, um herauszufinden, was Einkaufsteams wirklich brauchen, analysierst den Wettbewerb, damit wir genau wissen, wo wir gewinnen, und übersetzt beides in klare Feature-Anforderungen für das Tech-Team.

  • Finde heraus, wo unsere Kunden hängen bleiben. Mit modernen Product-Management-Methoden erkennst du, wo Kunden aktuell auf Engpässe stoßen, und schreibst Briefings, damit unsere Engineers sie beheben.

Qualifikation

Wir glauben nicht an perfekte Kandidat:innen oder starre Checklisten. Uns geht es um Antrieb, Neugier und die Fähigkeit, Dinge zu bauen. Die folgenden Punkte sind eine Orientierung, keine Hürde.

Must-haves

  • Motivation. Du bist hochmotiviert, fühlst dich in Unsicherheit wohl und passt dich schnell an. Die Studienrichtung spielt keine Rolle.

  • Eingeschrieben. Du bist aktuell in einem Bachelor- oder Masterstudium eingeschrieben (Urlaubssemester oder Gap Year willkommen).

  • Customer first. Du stellst den Kunden instinktiv an erste Stelle und baust echte, tragfähige Beziehungen zu Menschen auf.

  • Technisches Verständnis. Du musst unsere Plattform nicht selbst bauen, aber du verstehst die Grenzen von LLMs wie Context Windows, RAG und Tool Calling. Du weißt, dass Prompt Engineering nur der Anfang ist, und gräbst dich gern in Logs, um zu verstehen, warum ein Workflow fehlgeschlagen ist.

  • Storyteller. Du kannst etwas Komplexes so erklären, dass ein Raum voller skeptischer Einkäufer:innen daran glaubt.

  • AI-native. Du nutzt AI ganz selbstverständlich, um deine eigene Arbeit zu beschleunigen, experimentierst ständig und teilst, was wirklich funktioniert.

  • Sprachen. Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse (C2) und gute Englischkenntnisse (min. C1).

Nice-to-have

  • Erste Erfahrung in Beratung, Strategie, Produkt oder Engineering ist ein Plus.

Benefits

Als Praktikant:in bei qado hast du echten Impact und echte Verantwortung. Wir legen bei Praktikant:innen denselben Maßstab an wie bei Festangestellten. Deshalb holen wir nur Leute an Bord, denen wir zutrauen, Projekte eigenständig zu führen, und mit denen wir langfristig zusammenarbeiten wollen.

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den Gründern. Du bist Sparringspartner:in der Gründer, nicht mehrere Ebenen darunter. Du siehst und beeinflusst, wie das Unternehmen geführt wird.

  • Schnell echte Verantwortung. Deine Demos, Features und POVs gehen ab der ersten Woche live und landen bei echten Enterprise-Kunden.

  • Steile Lernkurve. Ein ehrlicher Einblick aus erster Reihe, was es braucht, um eines der ambitioniertesten AI-Unternehmen im Einkauf aufzubauen, über Produkt, Vertrieb und Tech hinweg.

  • Werde wirklich AI-native. In einem AI-Unternehmen nutzt und gestaltest du täglich Frontier-Tools und weißt danach genau, wie Unternehmen sie tatsächlich einführen.

  • Tools: High-End-Hardware und deine bevorzugten Produktivitätstools (Copilot, Cursor usw.). Wir zahlen, was dich produktiv macht.

  • Flexibilität: Standort München mit Hybrid-Modell.

  • Mentoring: Direkte, praktische Zusammenarbeit mit erfahrenen Gründern, die in deine Entwicklung investieren.

  • Faire Bezahlung und echte Perspektive: Eine solide Praktikumsvergütung und für die richtige Person eine klare Aussicht auf Übernahme in Vollzeit und frühe Führungsverantwortung.

Wir sind ein AI-native Startup aus München und bauen ein Geschäft in einem riesigen, bisher übersehenen Markt auf. In unserem kleinen, schnell wachsenden Team bist du von Anfang an mittendrin. Du arbeitest Tag für Tag direkt mit den Gründern, übernimmst echte Verantwortung statt Zuarbeit und bekommst Einblick in alle Bereiche, von Vertrieb und Strategie bis zur Produktentwicklung.

title: Founding ML Engineer (Spectrum)
descriptionHtml:
Software engineers and AI agents alike suffer from the same problem: finding that one person or place that will answer their tough, specific question. Many solutions promise to solve this with similarity search in vector databases. Unfortunately, finding the answer is often a puzzle with pieces to be collected across a myriad of contradictory sources and cannot be solved without surgical search and careful reasoning. 

Spectrum collects data from an organization’s code, docs, and issues, and organizes knowledge in a unified ontology that AI agents can efficiently search through and reason over. We aim to revolutionize the semantic layer space for software-building organizations and move beyond specs that fall out of sync with code, introducing a living spec – one that’s extracted from the whole system and used to keep it aligned. Spectrum is meant to be the single source of truth for all product and architectural knowledge.

Spectrum is a resident of JetBrains' startup incubator, with startup speed and autonomy, and backed by 25 years of developer tooling expertise. We are looking for a top-class ML Engineer who will help us shape the future of software development. You will own our AI and ML engineering stack and help define the research agenda for our team. Your technical vision and design decisions will directly shape the product and determine its success.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Designing and building the ML/LLM solution for data ingestion, knowledge extraction, retrieval, and subsequent reasoning.
  • Creating the datasets, metrics, and pipelines that drive measurable improvements across the system.
  • Architecting and improving agents for context retrieval, knowledge extraction, and data alignment, which includes prompt engineering, model selection, and inference optimization.
  • Establishing MLOps practices, including orchestration, observability, and experiment tracking.
  • Collaborating with the engineering team on system design and with JetBrains Research on the research agenda.
  • Defining hiring criteria, growing the ML team, and shaping the ML team culture.

We expect you to have:

  • A proven track record as an ML/AI Lead.
  • At least five years of experience in ML/AI systems, with at least two years focused on LLMs and generative AI.
  • A deep understanding of the LLM ecosystem, including model architectures and fine-tuning approaches.
  • Hands-on experience with:
    • Prompt engineering and LLM pipeline design, including evaluation.
    • Agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangSmith, smolagents, or an equivalent.
    • Vector databases and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns.
    • Deploying and scaling LLM-powered applications using APIs (e.g. OpenAI or Anthropic) or open-source models.
  • Strong Python skills – Kotlin knowledge would be a plus.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to diverse audiences.
  • Proficiency in English, both written and verbal. 

Our ideal candidate would have:

  • Experience with ontologies, knowledge graphs, or graph-based reasoning.
  • Experience in early-stage startups – you enjoy the zero-to-one phase.
  • The ability to think strategically about product-led AI, beyond just training models in isolation.
  • A background in code analysis, developer tools, or software engineering research.
  • Experience with multi-agent systems or complex agentic workflows.
  • Actively contributed to relevant open-source projects or publications.

What we offer

  • A competitive salary and JetBrains benefits.
  • A generous runway and corporate resources with startup autonomy.

title: Full-Stack Engineer - Data, Infrastructure & AI
descriptionHtml:
About Agent F

Agent F is building an autonomous finance function: software that takes on the work of keeping a company’s finances in order. That means bringing information together from different systems, recording transactions correctly, preparing useful reports, and helping people understand what needs their attention.

Today, much of this work depends on spreadsheets, repeated data entry and people checking one system against another. Our ambition is to make that work increasingly automatic, while keeping every number explainable and every consequential action under clear control.

We are building towards a complete business management system for growing companies. These founding roles will shape both the product and the way we build it.

About the role

You will be a full-stack engineer, shipping customer features across the interface, application services and database. Your particular strength will be the data and infrastructure that make those features dependable: how records are stored, how imports and background jobs run, and how information moves between Agent F and a customer’s other tools. You will help build and operate the whole product, with deeper ownership of this foundation.

This is hands-on full-stack engineering. A typical piece of work could involve extending a data model, implementing an application service, connecting it to a screen, testing it against a real database and following the release into production. You will also investigate slow reports, failed imports and jobs that stop halfway through, then improve the system so it handles those situations reliably.

That foundation also supports our AI work. As we add document extraction, connected customer knowledge and software that takes actions for customers, you will build the services and data access those features need. The immediate priority is dependable software that customers can use, with more capable automation developed around specific tasks.

What you will build and improve

  • Application services and customer features. Build the logic and application programming interfaces (APIs) that connect records, business rules and screens. Take features through implementation, testing, release and production support.

  • The database foundation. Design clear data models, enforce relationships and transaction boundaries, and improve slow queries. Manage schema changes through reviewed migrations, preserve financial history and keep each customer’s data isolated.

  • Imports and integrations. Connect accounting tools, business systems and spreadsheets to a consistent model. Validate incoming records, handle changing source formats, and check that imported totals and reports agree with the source.

  • Reliable background processing. Build scheduled jobs and workers that process work outside a user request. Handle retries without creating duplicates, resume interrupted runs, and make progress and failures visible to the team.

  • Performance and recovery. Diagnose expensive queries, processing bottlenecks and partial failures. Test changes against real databases, plan for growing workloads, and build procedures to recover processing safely with the platform engineer.

  • Practical AI automation. Add features such as extracting invoice fields or preparing an order from approved business data. Give models access through controlled services, check the result and require approval where needed. Develop connected customer knowledge when a feature needs those relationships, and measure whether it improves the result.

For example, a large customer import stops halfway through and the same records arrive again on the next run. You would make processing resume safely, prevent duplicate records, verify the resulting totals and expose the job’s status in the product. You would also investigate whether database queries or worker capacity caused the failure and ship the necessary fix.

What you bring

You have seven or more years of software engineering experience, including substantial ownership of production applications and data systems. You have designed relational data models, built services and processing pipelines, and stayed responsible for them after release. You are comfortable delivering across the stack and using AI tools in your daily work.

You can explain how you diagnosed a slow query, recovered a failed job or shipped a database change safely. You understand what happens when two requests arrive at once, a dependency becomes unavailable or a process restarts halfway through its work. You can follow a problem from a source record through the application to the result a customer sees.

Core experience

  • Full-stack development with TypeScript, Node.js, React and PostgreSQL, or closely comparable technologies.

  • Relational data modelling, SQL, query optimisation, indexes, transactions and reviewed database migrations.

  • Application services and APIs, including permissions, validation and handling concurrent requests.

  • Data imports, integrations and background jobs, including queues, safe retries and recovery from partial failures.

  • Production debugging, service monitoring and performance work on systems used by real customers.

  • Automated tests against real databases and other service dependencies.

  • Practical use of AI in software, with an understanding of how to check outputs and control access to customer data.

  • Daily use of AI coding agents, with direct responsibility for code review and verification.

  • A computer science or computer engineering degree, or equivalent practical depth.

Useful additional experience

Financial or operational systems where correctness and traceability matter; larger data migrations; cloud storage and container-based workloads. Experience putting document extraction or features using large language models (LLMs) into production would be valuable. Knowledge graphs, which connect related company records, and privately hosted or adapted models are useful as we develop that part of the product.

What early progress could look like

In your first months, you would take ownership of an existing service or data flow, understand how it runs in production and ship a customer-facing improvement through it. You would address a concrete reliability or performance problem, such as a slow report, a fragile integration or a job that cannot recover cleanly after interruption.

We would look for working features, faster and more predictable processing, fewer failed or manually repaired jobs, and useful tests and monitoring. An early automation feature could follow where the data and services are ready and its benefit can be measured.

Operational excellence and customer commitments

You take pride in a dependable application backbone: processing completes, records reconcile and customers can trust the results. When a job fails or figures disagree, you take ownership of the investigation and recovery. Missing transactions, duplicate entries or unexplained balance differences can be financial emergencies even while every service appears available. You assess the impact, contain affected processing, trace the cause and verify the repaired result before treating the incident as resolved.

Customer commitments shape how we work. You are willing to interrupt planned work, respond promptly and stay engaged when an urgent issue puts a service-level agreement (SLA), onboarding commitment or financial deadline at risk. That requires flexibility beyond normal working hours as part of agreed on-call coverage and coordinated incident response. You keep people informed and see the issue through to a verified recovery or an explicit handover. Afterwards, you improve the system so the same emergency becomes less likely.

How you will work

This is a senior founding role in a small team. You will own the application and data infrastructure for your work, and carry a full share of customer feature delivery. You will collaborate across infrastructure, operations and product design to deliver complete customer outcomes. You will use coding agents to implement changes and remain responsible for reviewing, testing and operating the result.

Everyone shares responsibility for the whole product and the customer outcome. You will pick up the most important work or whatever is on fire, including tasks outside your specialty. You take initiative, bring in the right expertise and stay involved until the problem is resolved. Customer impact and urgency determine where you focus.

The role is full-time and in-person in Berlin. German is not required.

  • With the coaching staff, establish a high performance culture through defining key values and expectations that the team should represent and follow

  • Manage team performance and behaviours, ensuring standards are upheld through appropriate recognition and disciplinary actions

  • Create an elite-tier performance environment with the practice approach, facilities, scheduling and team operations required to win at the highest level

  • Establish a platform and team culture that makes Fnatic a home players and staff aspire to be at and want to stay at, through player care and player experience worthy of their ambition

  • Establish a clear team structure and processes, and continually optimise them in collaboration with senior Esports management

  • Manage the League of Legends team budget, allocating resources effectively to deliver competitive success whilst supporting revenue generating activities

  • Oversee player contracts and obligations, monitoring the delivery of player obligations towards Fnatic, Riot Games and our partners

  • Champion a data and science led approach across recruitment, performance and decision-making, building on Fnatic's analytics capability and the tools that support it

  • Nurture relationships with title stakeholders on League of Legends specific topics, including Riot Games, tournament organisers, teams and player representatives, protecting the team’s interests throughout

  • Be a proactive ambassador for Fnatic across media, community and partner activities, including but not limited to interviews, content, community, and fan meetings

  • Ensure Fnatic brand, content and partnership strategies can be activated through player insights and access, and that the wider business is integrated with, and understood by, our League of Legends division

  • Lead on ad-hoc sporting projects as defined by CGO

We’re looking for:

  • Leadership experience within professional gaming or sports, with genuine accountability for results

  • Passion for esports and a strong understanding of the League of Legends scene

  • Competitive instinct and knowledge of what it takes to win

  • People management experience, including coaches and world-class athletes

  • Ability to inspire and educate the current and next generation of professional gamers, with a readiness to walk the extra mile for players when needed

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the confidence to represent Fnatic publicly and build trusted relationships with players, staff and fans

  • Commercial literacy, comfortable holding a budget and producing business cases

  • Proven ability to work with talent and people from diverse cultures and backgrounds

  • Excellent written and verbal English, other languages desirable

  • Based in Berlin, or willing to relocate


Diversity, Equity & Inclusion: #AlwaysFnatic

At Fnatic, we believe that a diverse mix of voices leads to better discussions, decisions, and outcomes for everyone. We strive to recruit and nurture an inclusive workforce who feel empowered every day to forge the future as part of the Black and Orange squad.

We know that applying for jobs can be daunting - but be assured that at Fnatic:

  • Who you are, and how you identify has no impact on our selection process

  • We understand no candidate will tick 100% of what our job descriptions are seeking, so if you’re missing a point here or there, we still want to hear from you

  • We're happy to consider reasonable adjustments where needed to fully participate in Fnatic’s recruitment experience - just let us know.

About us

Fnatic is a global esports performance brand headquartered in London, laser-focused on seeking out, levelling up and amplifying gamers and creators. Our history is unparalleled. Founded in 2004, we are the most successful esports brand of the last decade, winning more than 200 championships across 30 different games.

Today, driven by our ability to advance esports performance, Fnatic is the channel through which the most forward-thinking brands communicate with young people. We deliver industry-leading content, experiences and activations globally with bases in Berlin, Belgrade, Tokyo among others. Our pros and creators generate hundreds of millions of watch hours, showcasing our global partners to an audience of millions of fans across our social platforms.

Forging the future is in our DNA. We pioneered the intersection of street culture and esports with merch collaborations, and continue to lead the industry with the quality of our pro wear and fan apparel. After launching in 2016, our award-winning esports equipment (comprising mice, keyboards, headsets and pads) has sold to hundreds of thousands of gaming enthusiasts who want to play better.

Gaming is the place where music, fashion, sport and technology come together, and Fnatic is leading the charge.

title: Global People & Culture Director
descriptionHtml:
Strategic Mandate

The Global People Director will be a key architect of Cambridge Consultants’ transformation to inspire and lead a new era of deep tech innovation.   • Build an entrepreneurial, innovation‑driven culture where teams embrace calculated risk, experimentation, and rapid learning.
  • Shape an AI‑native organisation, equipping all employees with the mindset and fluency to leverage the latest AI tools.

  • Operationalise the cultural and behavioural expectations of our strategy through hiring, development, reward, leadership capabilities, and organisational design.

About the Role

You will act as a strategic partner to the executive team and senior leadership, linking the people agenda to our strategy. Driving transformational change in our People & Culture, to build a diverse talent engine tuned to innovation & partnership.


At the core of this role is shaping an entrepreneurial culture where people run toward bold innovation challenges - and build a diverse, high-performing talent engine that enables it. You’ll lead the Global People function, set direction for HR Business Partnering, Talent, L&D, EDI, and People Operations, and ensure integrated delivery across the employee lifecycle. You’ll be a critical partner to the executive, offering courageous challenge and clear thinking to align decisions with company goals.

Work pattern: Hybrid – role holder expected in office frequently & some international travel
Reports to: CHRO, Capgemini Invent with dotted line to Cambridge Consultants CEO
Direct Reports: 4 – HR Business Partnering, HR Ops, L&D, Recruitment

Key Responsibilities

1) Strategic Partnership & Organisational Leadership

  • Lead the Global People Team, managing the Heads of Functions to deliver the Global People Strategy
  • Partner with the executive team and senior leaders to translate business strategy into clear, outcome-based people plans that accelerate growth and innovation.
  • Shape the Executive Leadership Team as a cohesive team - improving decision quality, collaboration, and strategic alignment.
  • Lead org design and workforce planning (structure, capability, location strategy) for present and future needs in a global matrixed environment.

2) Culture, Engagement & Internal Communications

  • Champion a more entrepreneurial, experimentation-driven culture; reinforce psychological safety, ownership, and speed of learning.
  • Build and sustain high employee engagement; craft compelling narratives and communications that bring strategy to life.
  • Embed established feedback loops (listening strategy, pulse surveys) and turn insights into visible action.
  • Champion organisational simplification to improve pace, autonomy, and agility.

3) Talent Strategy & Leadership Development

  • Lead the development of a future skills blueprint, incl. deep tech, commercial partnering, and AI-native capabilities.

4) EDI / Inclusive Futures

5) Change & Transformation

6) Employer Brand & Marketing Partnership

7) People Analytics & Decision Support

  • Leverage HR analytics to diagnose business health (engagement, attrition, performance, diversity), forecast workforce needs, and inform decisions.
  • Build a data-driven culture within HR; improving people systems and data capture 

8) HR Solutions Delivery & Governance

  • Ensure integrated delivery across Talent Acquisition, HR Business Partnering, People Operations, L&D, Reward, and EDI.
  • Maintain high standards of compliance (employment law, data privacy), operational excellence, and scalable HR processes suitable for global growth.

Requirements & Qualifications

Experience

title: Graduate AI Transformation Lead
descriptionHtml:
TLDR: We’re looking for top 1%, high agency, AI-forward graduates to join the first graduate cohort at Resonance as AI Transformation Leads. We have recently raised one of the largest ever European seed rounds, with investment from Anthropic and Hg Capital, to deploy AI into the economy and rebuild businesses for the AI era. You’ll work at the frontier and solve real problems in an environment that champions ownership, autonomy and innovation at pace.

Who we are

Resonance is an applied AI company. We have recently raised one of the largest ever European seed rounds, with investment from Anthropic and Hg Capital. Our mission is to close the AI diffusion gap and rebuild businesses for the AI era. We're looking to hire Europe’s elite AI talent.

Why now

We believe the economic diffusion of AI is the major challenge of the next decade. Foundation models are advancing far faster than organisations can absorb them; the bottleneck is embedding AI deeply into the core processes of a company to drive an inflection in pace and create organisational advantage. Europe is falling behind on AI, and we exist to help its businesses build real, defensible advantage from it rather than simply adopting it.

The role

As a Graduate AI Transformation Lead, you’ll work on client teams from your first month, alongside experienced AI Transformation Leads and AI engineers, with real responsibility from day one. You’ll analyse how a business works, where time and money go, and where AI fundamentally changes the economics. You’ll build the models, business cases and story a leadership team will act on, and prototype new workflows yourself with Claude Code or similar. You’ll work side by side with engineers to define what gets built, test it with the people who will use it, and help the client’s teams adopt it. As one of our first graduate cohort, you’ll also help shape our graduate programme and how Resonance trains and grows.

Your first year: Structured training in AI, consulting and the industries we work in, with coaching from Senior AI Transformation Leads and the founding team. You’ll be on a client team from your first month, in a small team where you know everyone by name. Nobody expects you to know it all when you start: asking for help early is part of the job. You’ll start as a Junior Transformation Lead and typically move up a level within 18–24 months.

What we’re looking for: You have extreme agency, operate with urgency, and have consistently been among the very top performers of your peers. You’re finishing an undergraduate or master’s degree in a technical subject, such as engineering, computer science, mathematics, physics or another natural science, or a quantitative subject such as economics, or you graduated in one in the last two years, with top results from a top university. You structure problems clearly and are comfortable with numbers. You use AI every day and have built something with it, whether a project, a tool or an automation, and you’re curious about how businesses actually work. You can show you make things happen through internships, a society you led, a company you started or something you built. An internship in consulting, banking, private equity or a startup is a plus. If you don’t tick every box, apply anyway.

What we offer: Competitive total compensation plus equity. Real client work from your first month, learning from people who have shipped 30+ AI products and embedded AI into 50+ businesses. Every engagement ends with AI running in production and results you can measure. A team built to be one of the most talent-dense in Europe, and a chance to help close Europe’s AI gap, moving European businesses to the right side of the productivity chasm.

Logistics: London, 3+ days a week in the office or at client sites, mostly in the UK and Europe. English is our working language. We can sponsor visas for eligible candidates. Start date Summer 2027 (dates to be confirmed). We also offer Summer 2027 internships for students in the penultimate year of their degree.

Apply

Send your CV with your grades and a short note on something you've analysed or built with AI.

We hire people from every background and judge them on what they've built. If you don't tick every box, apply anyway.

Resonance is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. If you need adjustments at any stage, tell us and we'll make them.

title: GRC Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Remote from the UK, Germany, Austria, Poland, Montenegro or Serbia.

At Secfix, we’re at the forefront of automating security compliance in Europe. We help companies get and stay ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, and SOC 2 fast and easy and reduce hundreds of hours of manual work.

Secfix is run by a 100% remote team with hubs in Munich, Berlin and London. We’re a high-performing team looking for passionate, execution-focused, owners to help us automate security and compliance for modern companies and become the European compliance automation leader.

We’ve just raised our $12M Series A and are backed by top VCs, including Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital.

About the Role

We're hiring a GRC Specialist (Governance, Risk and Compliance) to strengthen our compliance function as Secfix scales into more frameworks, mid-market customers, and a growing compliance team.

This role sits at the intersection of compliance delivery, content, and team support. You'll own the compliance knowledge that lives inside our platform, run internal audits, support our customer success team, and act as the compliance voice for customers, auditors, and product.

You'll work closely with our co-founder & CISO and our CS Lead. This is a high-impact role with real influence on how Secfix delivers compliance: both as a service to customers and as content inside our app.

What You'll Do:

You will own one of the most important pillars of Secfix: the quality and breadth of our compliance offering. We don't (and can't afford to) micro-manage. We've built strong foundations and will give you full context on what works. You can test new approaches, but at the end of the day, you have full ownership of how you deliver results (with a strong support network from within and outside the company). You will:

  • Build and maintain compliance frameworks in the Secfix platform (ISO 27001, TISAX, SOC 2, GDPR, NIS 2, DORA, ISO 27017/27018, ISO 42001, C5, and more as we expand)

  • Own internal audits for our customers end to end, from kickoff through to the final report they take into their external audit

  • Keep several audits moving at once and keep every one on schedule

  • Implement ISO 27001 and adjacent frameworks end-to-end for customers

  • Own the quality of compliance content in the platform (including creating policies, automated checks, evidence templates, Compliance enable playbooks for our CSMs, security awareness trainings and more)

  • Close framework gaps and incorporate auditor feedback into both team practice and platform improvements

  • Partner with product and engineering to translate compliance gaps into structured product work

  • Collaborate closely with CS, Product, and Founders to align compliance, customer, and roadmap priorities

  • Deepen relationships with our existing certification partners and train auditors on the Secfix platform so they can confidently use it during customer audits

To be qualified for this role, you must have the following:

  • English (fluent) is a must for this role

  • 3+ years of hands‑on information security and GRC experience

  • Led at least 1 successful ISO 27001 certification projects as an implementer and/or auditor at a startup or mid-market company

  • You have run at least 2 internal audits before.

  • Hands on experience with a GRC platform like Secfix, or similar GRC platforms

  • Real depth in at least one framework beyond ISO 27001 (TISAX, SOC 2, GDPR, NIS2, or similar).

  • Strong project management skills with the ability to break down ambiguous initiatives into concrete deliverables, prioritizes ruthlessly, and ships

  • Excellent written communication, especially in producing clear, precise compliance content for diverse audiences (auditors, founders, engineers)

  • Strong ownership mindset: operates as an individual contributor without waiting for direction

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent hands-on technical experience.

Bonus points for:

  • Experience mentoring or coaching colleagues in a compliance, audit, or GRC context

  • Experience in a startup environment is a plus

  • A PECB ISO 27001 Lead Auditor certification or a direct equivalent

Interview Process:

  • Screening call with Talent team

  • Take-home Assessment

  • 1.5hr Assessment review and interview with our CS Lead and CEO

  • 45 min - Final Founder Interview with Co-Founders (CTO & CISO)

What we offer

  • Remote Work: 100% remote work with a virtual office in Gather.

  • Competitive Salary: Industry-competitive local salaries. We pay local rates that are at or above the market. We share this philosophy with GitLab.

  • Equity: Generous equity package – we’re all owners of Secfix and beneficiaries of our collective success.

  • Mentorship: We are backed by top VCs and accelerators and have direct access to world-class mentors.

  • Annual Retreat: Annual retreat to build connections and inspire ideas (this year we’re headed to Milan!).

title: Group Financial Accountant
descriptionHtml:
About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

Remote within the UK, or from our offices in London or Cambridge if you prefer.

The opportunity

CircuitHub is trying to solve a difficult problem: why can software engineers iterate almost instantly while hardware engineers can still wait weeks or months to manufacture a new design?

The company was founded by engineers who had experienced that frustration first-hand. What began as software to make ordering electronics easier has evolved into a much more ambitious manufacturing platform, combining software, robotics and automation to redesign the production process itself.

Today CircuitHub operates an automated electronics manufacturing platform serving hardware businesses across areas including robotics, autonomous systems and other advanced technology applications. Its proprietary Grid system is a factory-scale robotic assembly platform designed for rapid, high-mix electronics production.

The business is now scaling quickly. CircuitHub has raised $45 million to expand manufacturing capacity in both the US and Europe, building on operations in Massachusetts and its growing UK presence. Cambridge is becoming an increasingly important hub alongside London and the company's distributed team.

That growth creates a corresponding need to strengthen the operating infrastructure behind the company. Finance is one of the areas where CircuitHub has deliberately remained lean for longer than it probably should have.

Context: where finance is today

The finance team is led by a Finance Director and Management Accountant, both experienced, qualified accountants. This role brings dedicated financial accounting and technical reporting capability into the team, taking ownership of the books, the audit and the technical questions that come with a growing international group.

CircuitHub uses NetSuite to operate its inter-company financial model across the UK and US. A significant amount of day-to-day UK finance activity is outsourced, while the internal team takes greater ownership of the larger US operation, group reporting and consolidation. This role will be the main point of contact for the outsourced firm, reviewing their work and making sure it meets the standard the group needs, while also working across the US side and the wider mechanics of an international business.

Just as importantly, CircuitHub is thinking carefully about what the next generation of finance roles should look like. AI and automation are already being deployed across the company, including in areas where repetitive finance work can be made considerably more efficient.

That makes strong technical accountants even more important. CircuitHub needs people who understand the numbers well enough to judge whether automated output is right, and who can use technology to improve how finance works without weakening control.

That combination of technical accounting, real ownership and a technology-enabled way of working is a central part of the opportunity.

The mandate

The Group Financial Accountant will take ownership of CircuitHub’s financial accounting across the UK and US. That means understanding how the books are put together, running a reliable close and being the person the Finance Director, the auditors and the outsourced accounting firm rely on for accurate, well-supported numbers.

Alongside the core accounts, the role will lead on technical accounting as the business scales. CircuitHub is investing heavily in manufacturing capacity and moving towards more flexible commercial models, which raises questions around revenue recognition, capitalisation and intercompany that need a clear owner.

The candidate must be willing to get their hands dirty to get a full appreciation of the sales cycle & work with the Finance Director to improve our systems and controls to improve our collection cycle, reducing DSO & further automation for our credit offering.

The candidate should have a good technical understanding in accounting that can lead to developing financial operations without complicating or delaying the reporting process. Developing our systems to improve the speed and efficiency of areas such as revenue recognition, R&D capitalisation & the consolidation process.

What you will work on

The precise balance will evolve with the candidate, but the remit is expected to include:

  • Financial accounting and close. Own month-end, including journals, accruals, prepayments and balance sheet reconciliations, with a clear understanding of how the accounts fit together.

  • Audit and statutory reporting. Act as the first point of contact for the auditors, manage their requests and prepare supporting schedules under UK GAAP and IFRS.

  • Technical accounting. Lead projects such as IFRS 15 revenue recognition, the capitalisation policy and the treatment of intercompany transactions as the business and its commercial models develop.

  • Group reporting. Support reporting across the UK and US entities, including intercompany reconciliations, and contribute to group consolidation in NetSuite where experience allows.

  • Outsourced provider management. Manage the relationship with the UK outsourced accounting firm, reviewing their output and holding it to the standard the group needs.

  • NetSuite and finance systems. Work directly in NetSuite and across the different systems and platforms that feed into it. Understand how data moves through the business rather than treating the accounting system in isolation.

  • AI and automation. Review and take ownership of automated and AI-generated finance output, making sure it is accurate and properly controlled, and help identify where further automation makes sense.

What success looks like

The first objective is to be a safe pair of hands. That means solving outstanding technical issues, taking ownership of monthly & quarterly close, a well-run audit and numbers the Finance Director and the team can trust without needing to revisit them.

From there, success means taking ownership of the technical agenda: a clear approach to revenue recognition as commercial models change, a robust capitalisation policy as CircuitHub invests in capacity, and clean intercompany accounting across the UK and US.

Over time, the finance team should have the capacity to report more frequently, stronger oversight of outsourced work and less technical accounting sitting with the Finance Director simply because nobody else can own it.

Processes should improve as well as move faster. Automation should remove low-value work without weakening financial control.

This is a role to build into over time. The scope will grow with the finance function and with the contribution the individual makes to it. As the business scales, the role is expected to grow into Group Financial Controller.

The person we are looking for

CircuitHub is looking for a qualified or near-qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or CIMA) with strong technical foundations. The specific qualification matters less than acumen, drive and personal qualities.

You are likely to have trained in practice, whether at a Big 4 or a top 20 firm, and be looking for your first move into an operating business. Alternatively, you may already be working in industry, in which case you will be qualified or close to qualifying.

The strongest signals are:

  • Relevant exposure. Experience getting the most out of NetSuite, working in a finance team to produce accounting information & ability to work autonomously and conscientiously to meet deadlines.

  • Technical grounding. Strong knowledge of UK GAAP and IFRS and a clear understanding of how a set of accounts is put together.

  • Technology fluency. You are comfortable working across systems and genuinely interested in how AI is changing finance. You see automation as a tool, not a substitute for judgement.

  • Practical curiosity. When something does not reconcile or a process feels unnecessarily difficult, your instinct is to understand why.

  • Commitment to building. You are motivated by breadth and ownership, and you want to build something over time in a growing business.

  • Interest in the business. CircuitHub sits at the intersection of software, robotics and physical manufacturing. You do not need an electronics background, but an interest in technology and how real products are built will make the environment much more compelling.

Why CircuitHub

This is a chance to join a profitable, fast-growing robotics and manufacturing business at a pivotal stage of scale, in a role with genuine technical ownership.

You will work closely with experienced qualified accountants and gain a breadth of exposure that is rare this early in an industry career: revenue recognition, capitalisation, intercompany, audit and reporting across a UK and US group.

You will also build for where finance is going next. CircuitHub is already using AI, automation and connected systems across the business, creating the opportunity to combine strong technical accounting with skills in systems, data and automation.

For someone with the capability and drive, there is real scope to grow as CircuitHub scales and the finance function builds out around it.

Pay

£75k–£85k, depending on experience, plus equity.

Compensation: £75K – £85K • Offers Equity

title: Growth Engineer (Intern)
descriptionHtml:
👷🏻‍♀️ What we do 👷🏻‍♀️

At Emidat, we are building the first climate-native product management system for building material manufacturers.

Emidat aims to decarbonise building materials, making up 11% of global GHG emissions. We collect data from physical production processes, generate a digital product passport with verified environmental data and make it usable along the value chain. In short: One solution to assess, design, buy, sell and manage products - with environmental impact at the core.

Embodied carbon is emitted on day zero and can never be reduced later, while global floor area is set to double by 2060. From January 2026, EU regulation (CPR) requires verified environmental data. 430,000 manufacturers will need it, and only about 2,500 have it today. That gap is our market.

Find out more about us, the team and our values here.

What you will work on

Your mission

Drive initiatives that grow Emidat. In Growth we prioritise by one question: does this bring in new customers? As a Growth Engineer Intern you work across our four growth functions that sits closest to that answer; 1. Growth Engineering, 2. Growth Marketing, 3. Sales Development and 4. Partnerships

Topics you might work on: our automated campaign planning and lead development process, and the automations behind it. Our mapping of the total addressable market (TAM) and the GTM analysis sheet we use to decide which segments and countries to go after. Our industry get-togethers, for example expert exchanges and C-level breakfasts, from the invite list to the follow-up. LinkedIn posts and customer case studies, which means talking to manufacturers who use Emidat and turning what they tell you into material our sales team can send.

This internship is ideal for someone who has future aspirations to ‘found’ a company. Building a revenue function is one of the most difficult parts of founding, and during your internship, you’ll get insights into how demand is created, how a pipeline is built, and how AI actually optimises a go-to-market team. You will work on initiatives with the leads of each growth function, including our Head of Growth. We expect you to work independently, form your own view on what to prioritise, and challenge us when you think we have it wrong.

 

During your Internship, you will:

Joining our Growth team involves:

  • Own our Campaign Process: Run and sharpen the automated workflow that qualifies and enriches our target accounts, and take responsibility for the pipeline our SDR team works from.

  • Map our Market: Extend our TAM mapping into every new geography we enter, and keep our view of the relevant manufacturers, associations and registries current - so the commercial team always plans against a reliable picture of who is worth targeting.

  • Turn Data into Decisions: Build and maintain the reporting our team steers by, from campaign performance to pipeline health. Translate data into clear, actionable insights and own the data quality that makes those numbers trustworthy.

  • Organise our industry get-togethers: Organise formats like the BAU Dinner, our C-level AI Breakfasts and the Climate Native Summit end-to-end - guest list, invitations, on-site logistics and follow-up - turning each one into a reliable source of senior conversations.

  • Build Our Market Presence: Draft posts for our company page and keep our content calendar running: webinars and event announcements, product news, new joiners, and the pieces that build our positioning in the market.

Internal Tech Stack:

CRM: Hubspot

Automation: N8N, Clay

Outreach: Lemlist, LinkedIn Sales Navigator

AI Tooling: Claude Co-work/Code
Content & design: LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Figma

Messaging: Slack & Google Workspace

What you will bring to this role

Minimum Requirements

  • Language: Fluent (C2/Native) in German and business fluent (C1+) in English.

  • Data-Driven System Integration: Proven ability to interpret complex performance data, generating actionable insights that directly inform strategy. You must be able to effectively bridge data analysis with our internal tech stack to drive business outcomes.

  • Proactive & Strategic Problem-Solving: A track record of independently identifying and resolving operational bottlenecks in processes, leading to measurable improvements in efficiency.

  • Operational Excellence & Project Ownership: Exceptional organisational skills with a demonstrated capability to manage multiple, high-priority projects concurrently, ensuring successful delivery within tight deadlines.

Nice to have’s

  • Educational Background: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a relevant field.

  • Expertise in Growth Stack Technologies: Hands-on experience and familiarity with core automation, analytics, and CRM systems, including specific platforms like Hubspot, N8N, Clay, Lemlist, and Make.

  • Content & Social: Experience running a company's or organisation's LinkedIn presence, or writing experience with an audience behind it - a newsletter or blog of your own.

  • Start-up Experience: Experience in a commercial or operational role in a startup or scaleup.

     

How we support you

You will work with

title: Growth Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Fyxer

Since launching in May 2024 we've grown to $30 million in ARR. Fyxer is building an AI executive assistant that handles emails, scheduling and follow-up, freeing people in client-facing roles to focus on their customers.

The Mission

At Fyxer, we believe the only sustainable competitive advantage for a startup is the quality and speed of execution.

 

We are looking for a full-stack product thinker who uses research, data, and experimentation to drive better bets, faster learning, and stronger commercial outcomes. We’re not looking for someone to write specs and hand over insights. We want someone who helps us think better and decide better.

You’ll drive product vision and strategy of a product domain alongside our product, growth and leadership teams.


The Role

You’ll drive product vision and strategy of a product domain / category design alongside our product / growth and leadership teams.

You will operate at speed. We care about generating signals quickly, making informed decisions, and learning fast. You are comfortable working with imperfect information and tightening thinking as you go.

You will have significant autonomy. We expect strong judgment, clear communication, and ownership of outcomes and a fullstack background around A/B experimentation and everything that comes with it.

  

What you will own:

You will own the quality of our product bets and the speed at which we learn.

  • Turn ambiguity into direction. Take messy signals from customers, product data, and the market and translate them into clear problem framing and product strategy.

  • Work directly with engineers. You will partner closely with engineers and founders from the start of an initiative, shaping solutions together rather than handing over specs.

  • Use the right tools to validate ideas and reduce risk: interviews, prototypes, experiments, product analytics, fake doors, usability testing, and behavioural analysis

  • Ship, learn, and iterate quickly. Move product bets from idea to shipped product to measurable outcomes, continuously tightening the loop between learning and building.

  • Raise the bar of product thinking across the team by coaching others, introducing scalable frameworks, and helping the team stay close to customers

  

Who You Are

  • Expert: You are an expert in your domain specialization that everyone could learn from including our other PM’s

  • Systems thinker: You understand customer journeys, funnels, and feedback loops. You connect user behaviour to outcomes and revenue impact, not just isolated features.

  • Engineering partner: You work closely with engineers and founders, translating user insight into clear problem framing and practical tradeoffs. You influence what we build through evidence and clarity.

  • Decision oriented: You know when there is enough signal to move. You help others clarify thinking, sharpen hypotheses, and make confident calls under uncertainty.

  • Capability builder: You design product systems that compound over time rather than one off projects. Your work levels up how we do product and discovery across the company, and you introduce frameworks, coach others, and build repeatable learning loops.

 

Why Fyxer?

We are intentional about our team. We believe a small, exceptional team working with extreme focus will always outperform a large, bloated organization.

  • Autonomy: We hire people who want ownership and then we actually give it to them.

  • Scope: This is a rare opportunity to join a high-growth rocket ship at the foundational stage..

  • Velocity: You will be fast-tracked into senior responsibilities far earlier than at a traditional company.


#LI-FYX
